'''Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba''' ({{IPA|es|alˈfɾeðo ˈpeɾeθ ruβalˈkaβa}}; 28 July 1951 – 10 May 2019) was a Spanish statesman, politician and [[chemist]] who served as [[First Deputy Prime Minister of Spain|Deputy Prime Minister of Spain]] from 2010 to 2011, and previously as [[Ministry of Education (Spain)|Minister of Education]] from 1992 to 1993, as [[Minister of the Presidency]] from 1993 to 1996, as [[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|Minister of the Interior]] from 2006 to 2011 and as acting [[Ministry of Defence (Spain)|Minister of Defence]] between May and June 2008.<ref>[https://www.foxnews.com/world/spain-rubalcaba-official-who-helped-end-militant-eta-dies Spain: Rubalcaba, official who helped end militant ETA, dies]</ref>

He also served as [[Leader of the Opposition (Spain)|Leader of the Opposition]] from 2011 to 2014 and as Secretary-General of the [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party]] (PSOE) from 2012 to 2014. He obtained a PhD in Organic Chemistry at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]].

== Biography ==

=== Early life and academic career ===
He was born in the village of Solares, in the [[Medio Cudeyo]] municipality, [[Santander, Spain|Santander]] province. He moved aged 3 to [[Salamanca (Madrid)|Salamanca]], Madrid, with his family and studied at the [[Colegio del Pilar (Madrid)|Colegio del Pilar]].<ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://cantabrialiberal.com/opinion/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-el-ministro-de-solares-por-pedro-arce,491186.html|journal=Cantabria Liberal|date=10 May 2019|first=Pedro|last=Arce|title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba el ministro de Solares, por Pedro Arce}}</ref> His father was an [[Iberia (airline)|Iberia]] pilot, and his grandfather was a [[Republican faction (Spanish Civil War)|Republican]] captain.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Torices |first=Alfonso |date=2011-11-21 |title=El vendaval pudo con el esprínter |url=https://www.elnortedecastilla.es/rc/20111121/mas-actualidad/espana/vendaval-pudo-esprinter-201111211150.html |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=El Norte de Castilla |language=es}}</ref> He joined the [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party|PSOE]] in 1974, and, being a keen athlete at school, ran the 100 metres in 10.9 seconds at the national championships.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-03-04 |title=Rubalcaba era un gran esprínter |trans-title=Rubalcaba was always a great sprinter |url=http://www.laopinioncoruna.es/galicia/2011/05/30/rubalcaba-gran-esprinter/500193.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304064556/http://www.laopinioncoruna.es/galicia/2011/05/30/rubalcaba-gran-esprinter/500193.html |archive-date=2016-03-04 |access-date=2015-10-20 |website=La Opinión Coruña}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-11 |title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, un velocista que sufrió con el caso Marta Domínguez |url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/atletismo/20190511/462169637123/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-un-velocista-que-sufrio-con-el-caso-marta-dominguez.html |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=Mundo Deportivo |language=es}}</ref> He married chemist Pilar Goya, a childhood friend with whom he reconnected at university.<ref>{{Cite web |last=20minutos |date=2019-05-11 |title=Pilar Goya, toda una vida al lado de Rubalcaba |trans-title=Pilar Goya, all her life at the side of Rubalcaba |url=https://www.20minutos.es/noticia/3637710/0/pilar-goya-viuda-rubalcaba/ |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=[[20minutos]] |language=es}}</ref> He achieved a chemistry doctorate at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]], and in his previous academic career, he became a senior lecturer in [[organic chemistry]] in 1984.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mateos |first=Abdón |date=2019-05-11 |title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, un hombre de Estado para tiempos de crisis. Apunte de urgencia |trans-title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, a man of the State for times of crisis. Emergency note |url=https://www.elobrero.es/opinion/item/28075-alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-un-hombre-de-estado-para-tiempos-de-crisis-apunte-de-urgencia.html |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190511201447/https://www.elobrero.es/opinion/item/28075-alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-un-hombre-de-estado-para-tiempos-de-crisis-apunte-de-urgencia.html |archive-date=2019-05-11 |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=[[El Obrero]]}}</ref> He also worked at the [[University of Konstanz]] and the [[University of Montpellier]], where his main contributions to the scientific field were his studies on [[reaction mechanism]]s.<ref>{{Cite news |date=1992-06-23 |title=Rubalcaba, un químico mediador en los conflictos de Educación |trans-title=Rubalcaba, a mediating chemist in conflicts of education |url=https://www.abc.es/archivo/periodicos/abc-madrid-19920623-22.html |url-access=subscription |work=[[ABC (newspaper)|ABC]] |pages=22}}</ref>

Rubalcaba's early involvement in politics began in the wake of the murder of fellow Colegio del Pilar alumni {{ill|Enrique Ruano|es}} by the Francoist secret police.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.publico.es/espana/estudiar-quimica-meterse-politica-y.html|website=[[Público (Spain)|Público]]|title=Estudiar química, meterse en política y correr los 100|date=5 November 2021|last=Avendaño|first=Antonio}}</ref>

He spoke fluent Spanish, English and French, and had a working knowledge of German from his time lecturing at Konstanz.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2011-10-07 |title=Rubalcaba quiere que las cadenas de televisión emitan en inglés como primera opción su programación infantil |trans-title=Rubalcaba wants TV networks to broadcast their children's programmes in English first |url=https://www.europapress.es/nacional/noticia-20n-rubalcaba-quiere-cadenas-television-emitan-ingles-primera-opcion-programacion-infantil-20111007152557.html |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=[[Europa Press]]}}</ref>

He represented [[Toledo (Spanish Congress Electoral District)|Toledo]] in Congress from 1993 to 1996, [[Madrid (Spanish Congress Electoral District)|Madrid]] from 1996 until 2004, [[Cantabria (Spanish Congress Electoral District)|Cantabria]] from 2004 to 2008 and, despite not being [[Andalusian people|Andalusian]], was put forward for the [[safe seat|safe parliamentary seat]] of [[Cádiz (Spanish Congress Electoral District)|Cádiz]] in the 2008 election, which he won.<ref>[https://www.elperiodico.com/es/politica/20190510/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-biografia-7447062 Rubalcaba, el político que lo fue casi todo] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190514135947/https://www.elperiodico.com/es/politica/20190510/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-biografia-7447062 |date=2019-05-14 }} {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[https://elpais.com/politica/2019/05/10/actualidad/1557481683_565547.html Adiós a un político de Estado] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[https://www.eitb.eus/es/noticias/politica/detalle/6394607/biografia-alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-perfil-historico-dirigente-psoe/ Rubalcaba, el ministro del Interior que vivió el fin de la violencia de ETA] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

=== González cabinet ===
With [[Felipe González]]'s election win in [[1982 Spanish general election|1982]], Rubalcaba took on various posts in the [[Ministry of Education (Spain)|Education Ministry]], including Director of the Technical Cabinet for the Secretary of State for Universities and Investigation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-05-13 |title=Rubalcaba, el ministro que impulsó la Logse |url=https://www.magisnet.com/2019/05/rubalcaba-el-ministro-que-impulso-la-logse/ |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=Magisnet |language=es}}</ref>

Rubalcaba was appointed [[Secretary of State for Education (Spain)|Secretary of State for Education]] in 1986 and in 1992 he was promoted to [[Ministry of Education (Spain)|Minister of Education and Science]]<ref>[https://elpais.com/diario/1992/06/23/espana/709250419_850215.html Javier Solana y Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, nuevos ministros de Asuntos Exteriores y de Educación] {{in lang|es}}</ref> by [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Felipe González]]. After the [[1993 Spanish general election|1993 general election]] he was appointed [[Minister of the Presidency|Minister of the Presidency and Relations with the Cortes]] and [[Spokesperson of the Government of Spain|Spokesperson of the Government]]<ref>[https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20190510/462136945465/muere-alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-ictus.html Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba fallece a los 67 años] {{in lang|es}}</ref> until 1996 when his party lost the [[1996 Spanish general election|general election]]. He was re-elected as the representative for [[Madrid (Congress of Deputies constituency)|Madrid]]. As a Minister he had to face the accusations that involved the government of Felipe González with the [[GAL (paramilitary group)|GAL paramilitary group]], as well as to use his negotiation skills to get both parties around the table when neither party co-operated.<ref>[https://elpais.com/diario/1995/01/10/espana/789692411_850215.html "Ni toleré el GAL ni lo consentí ni lo organicé"] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[https://elpais.com/diario/1995/07/21/espana/806277614_850215.html Damborenea acusa a González de autorizar los GAL] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

=== Spell in opposition ===
In 1997, Rubalcaba was appointed as a member of the [[Spanish Socialist Workers' Party|PSOE]] executive, and his inclusion was seen as a sign of his role to play in the next era outside of government. His bipartisanship made him one of the main Congress figures keeping in touch with [[ETA (separatist group)|ETA]] following a truce agreed in 1999. When [[José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero]] was elected leader in 2000, Rubalcaba joined the party's federal committee, playing a key role in the party's road map back to government. He brought the PSOE and [[People's Party (Spain)|PP]] together in December 2000 to agree to work with each other to fight against ETA.

=== Interior minister and deputy prime minister ===
For the [[2004 Spanish general election]], Rubalcaba was responsible for the electoral strategy of the [[PSOE]]. Some political analysts attribute him a decisive role in the socialist victory.<ref>{{Cite web |last=infoLibre |date=2019-05-10 |title=Rubalcaba: el socialista que lo fue todo menos presidente del Gobierno |url=https://www.infolibre.es/politica/rubalcaba-socialista-presidente-gobierno_1_1170300.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190510153451/https://www.infolibre.es/noticias/politica/2019/05/09/rubalcaba_uno_los_artifices_del_fin_eta_que_fracaso_asalto_moncloa_94830_1012.html |archive-date=2019-05-10 |access-date=2019-05-11 |website=infoLibre |language=es}}</ref>

After the investiture of the [[Cortes Generales]], Pérez Rubalcaba was appointed Leader of the Socialist Group in the [[Congress of Deputies]]. On 11 April 2006 he replaced [[José Antonio Alonso]] as head of the [[Ministry of the Interior (Spain)|Ministry of the Interior]]. It was in this ministry where he gained popularity within his party, thanks, among other measures, to the change of direction in the fight against terrorism that led to the end of the violence of [[Euskadi Ta Askatasuna|ETA]]. However, several media and political parties accused Rubalcaba of being involved in the ''Faisán case'', about an extortion network of ETA, a fact that has not been verified.<ref>[https://www.abc.es/20110216/opinion-editoriales/abcp-caso-faisan-caso-rubalcaba-20110216.html «El «Caso Faisán», «Caso Rubalcaba»] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

After the socialist victory in the [[2008 Spanish general election|general elections of 2008]], Pérez Rubalcaba kept his ministerial portfolio, remaining Interior Minister during the IX Legislature.<ref>[https://elpais.com/elpais/2008/04/12/actualidad/1207988223_850215.html Los 17 ministerios del nuevo Gobierno de Zapatero] {{in lang|es}}</ref> Between 20 May and 30 June 2008 he assumed the duties of [[Ministry of Defence (Spain)|Minister of Defence]] temporarily when [[Carme Chacón]] was on maternity leave, combining these functions with his work as Interior Minister.<ref>[https://elpais.com/diario/2008/05/20/espana/1211234416_850215.html Rubalcaba suplirá a Chacón en Defensa durante la baja maternal] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[https://www.boe.es/boe/dias/2008/05/20/pdfs/A23789-23789.pdf REAL DECRETO 860/2008, de 19 de mayo, por el que se dispone la suplencia de la Ministra de Defensa.] {{in lang|es}}</ref>
[[File:Fernández de la Vega traspasa la cartera de vicepresidente primero y portavoz del Gobierno a Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba. Pool Moncloa. 21 de octubre de 2010.jpeg|thumb|left|200px|Rubalcaba succeeding Fernández de la Vega]]

On 21 October 2010 he replaced [[María Teresa Fernández de la Vega]] as [[Deputy Prime Minister of Spain|Deputy Prime Minister]] and Spokesperson of the Government, combining this with his responsibilities as head of the Interior portfolio.<ref>[https://www.hola.com/actualidad/2010102046070/zapatero/remodelacion/gobierno/ Zapatero remodela su Gobierno, con Rubalcaba como vicepresidente primero] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20101020/54052000132/zapatero-cede-y-situa-a-rubalcaba-como-nuevo-hombre-fuerte-de-su-gobierno.html Zapatero cede y sitúa a Rubalcaba como nuevo hombre fuerte de su Gobierno] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

On 10 January 2011, ETA declared that their September 2010 ceasefire would be permanent and verifiable by international observers.<ref name="grauniad">[https://www.theguardian.com/world/2011/jan/10/eta-declares-permanent-ceasefire ETA declares permanent ceasefire], The Guardian, 10 January 2011</ref> On 20 October 2011, the Basque terrorist group, after 43 years of activity and more than 800 deaths in Spain, announced its definitive cessation of violence.<ref>[https://elpais.com/politica/2011/10/19/actualidad/1319056094_153776.html ETA pone fin a 43 años de terror] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

As minister he also had to face the high accident rate on Spanish roads. His attempts to solve it were the most successful in history in reducing the number of fatalities, and became a benchmark at European level.<ref>[https://elpais.com/politica/2019/05/12/actualidad/1557661908_620483.html Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, el ministro que puso freno a los accidentes de tráfico] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

=== Premiership candidate ===
As it became increasingly likely that Zapatero was not going to seek re-election, Rubalcaba became the favourite to succeed him, with [[Carme Chacón]] as his only rival in the primaries. Nevertheless, in May 2011, Chacón announced that she was withdrawing from the race, and in June Rubalcaba was chosen unopposed as the PSOE's candidate for Prime Minister at the [[2011 Spanish general election|2011 general election]].<ref>[https://www.economist.com/europe/2011/04/07/exit-plan Exit plan:The Socialists contemplate who would be their best new leader] The Economist 7 April 2011</ref> On 8 July 2011, he resigned from his duties in the government in order to focus on the election campaign. The PSOE lost the 2011 elections in a landslide, getting the worst results in PSOE's history.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Fernández |first=Alberto |date=2011-11-20 |title=Rubalcaba bate la peor marca del PSOE en 30 años |url=http://www.rtve.es/noticias/20111120/sprinter-rubalcaba-bate-peor-marca-del-psoe/476858.shtml |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=[[Radiotelevisión Española|RTVE]] |language=es}}</ref> Later studies, however, suggested that Zapatero's second government and its handling of the [[Great Recession]] turned off potential voters more than Rubalcaba as a potential Prime Minister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Dosek |first=Tomas |date=2013-11-01 |title=Why did PSOE lose in the general elections in Spain in 2011? An analysis of electoral behaviour |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/264046885 |website=[[ResearchGate]]}}</ref>

He applied to succeed José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero as PSOE's General Secretary and won the vote, held on 6 February 2012.<ref>[https://www.lavanguardia.com/politica/20120203/54248586232/congreso-psoe-rubalcaba-chacon.html En directo: Rubalcaba cierra el congreso] {{in lang|es}}</ref> He received 487 votes against 465 for Carme Chacón.<ref>elperiodicodeaqui.com http://www.elperiodicodeaqui.com/noticia/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-gana-carme-chacon-por-22-votos-diferencia/15251 {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714230131/http://www.elperiodicodeaqui.com/noticia/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-gana-carme-chacon-por-22-votos-diferencia/15251 |date=2014-07-14 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.rtve.es/alacarta/videos/congreso-del-psoe-2012/perfil-alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-nuevo-secretario-general-del-psoe/1313136/ Perfil de Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, nuevo secretario general del PSOE] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

=== Resignation and later life ===
[[File:Isabel Díaz Ayuso en la presentación del libro de David Alvaro " CATALUÑA, La construcción de un relato". (33066662038).jpg|thumb|left|220px|Rubalcaba in January 2019 with [[Josep Piqué]] (right)]]
Due to the bad results of the party in the [[2014 European Parliament election]], Rubalcaba resigned on 26 May 2014.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2014/05/26/53832a0b268e3e1f488b4571.html |title=Rubalcaba se va |language=es |first=Luis Ángel |last=Sanz |date=26 May 2014 |access-date=10 May 2019 |location=Madrid |newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]] |publisher=[[Unidad Editorial Información General]] S.L.U.}}</ref> He delayed his resignation for a few months to ensure his party voted 'yes' to [[Abdication of Juan Carlos I|Juan Carlos I's abdication]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rayón |first=Fernando |date=2019-05-13 |title=Muere Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba: Me viene fatal, pero contad conmigo |url=https://www.larazon.es/espana/me-viene-fatal-pero-contad-conmigo-FL23285918 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190513170233/https://www.larazon.es/espana/me-viene-fatal-pero-contad-conmigo-FL23285918 |archive-date=2019-05-13 |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=[[La Razón (Spain)|La Razón]]}}</ref> After a leadership election, Rubalcaba was succeeded by the newly elected Secretary General [[Pedro Sánchez (politician)|Pedro Sánchez]] on 13 July 2014.

In September 2016 it was announced that Pérez Rubalcaba would return to his position as Chemistry professor at the [[Complutense University of Madrid]].<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2014/09/29/54299741268e3edc6b8b4579.html |title=Rubalcaba comenzará su actividad docente en la Complutense con seminarios de Química Orgánica |language=es |author=Servimedia |date=29 September 2014 |access-date=10 May 2019 |location=Madrid |newspaper=[[El Mundo (Spain)|El Mundo]]}}</ref> He also joined the editorial board of ''[[El País]]'', of which he was part until July 2018.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.eldiario.es/politica/Alfredo-Perez-Rubalcaba-editorial-Pais_0_556795079.html |title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba se incorpora al consejo editorial de El País |language=es |date=8 September 2016 |access-date=10 May 2019 |newspaper=[[El Diario (Spain)|El Diario]]}}</ref>

Rubalcaba's successor Pedro Sánchez offered him the chance to run as PSOE candidate for the Mayor of Madrid in the [[2019 Madrid City Council election]], but he declined.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://elpais.com/politica/2018/12/26/actualidad/1545820669_734917.html |title=Rubalcaba rechaza la oferta de Pedro Sánchez para ser candidato al Ayuntamiento de Madrid |language=es |location=Madrid |date=26 December 2018 |access-date=10 May 2019 |newspaper=[[El País]] |publisher=[[Prisa]]}}</ref>

==Death==
Rubalcaba was admitted to the Puerta de Hierro Hospital, in [[Majadahonda]], on 8 May 2019 when he had suffered a severe stroke after teaching in the university.<ref>{{cite news
|url=https://elpais.com/elpais/2019/05/09/inenglish/1557416217_275386.html|work=El País|title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, a key figure in Spanish politics, dies aged 67|date=10 May 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|archive-date=24 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191224170343/https://elpais.com/elpais/2019/05/09/inenglish/1557416217_275386.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://elpais.com/politica/2019/05/08/actualidad/1557336544_377047.html |title=Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, ingresado en estado grave tras haber sufrido un ictus|language=es|first=José |last=Marcos|date=9 May 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|location=Madrid|newspaper=El País|publisher=Prisa}}</ref> He died two days later, aged 67. The PSOE cancelled all the acts of the first day of the campaign for local elections.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.elmundo.es/espana/2019/05/10/5cd452f521efa011368b45e7.html|title=Muere Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba a los 67 años tras sufrir un ictus|first=Marisol|last=Hernández|date=10 May 2019|access-date=10 May 2019|newspaper=El Mundo|language=es|publisher=Unidad Editorial Información General S.L.U.}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Loren
|first=Eduardo|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.es/entry/la-vida-politica-de-rubalcaba-en-imagenes_es_5cd45049e4b054da4e858b33?ncid=other_homepage_tiwdkz83gze|work=Huffington Post|title=La vida política de Rubalcaba en imágenes|trans-title=The political life of Rubalcaba in pictures|language=Spanish|date=10 May 2019}}</ref><ref>[https://www.nytimes.com/2019/05/12/obituaries/alfredo-perez-rubalcaba-dies.html Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, 67, Dies; Helped End Basque Terrorism]</ref> He had a funeral with state honours at the Congress of Deputies.<ref>[http://www.rtve.es/alacarta/videos/especiales-informativos/reyes-despiden-rubalcaba-congreso-diputados/5193638/ Los reyes despiden a Rubalcaba en el Congreso de los Diputados] {{in lang|es}}</ref><ref>[https://elpais.com/elpais/2019/05/10/album/1557505993_222929.html La capilla ardiente de Alfredo Pérez Rubalcaba, en imágenes] {{in lang|es}}</ref>

On 3 November 2020, Interior Minister [[Fernando Grande-Marlaska]] announced that he would posthumously award Rubalcaba with the police force's highest honours, to commemorate his work against organised crime and terrorism, in particular against ETA during Zapatero's government.<ref>{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-11-03 |title=La Policía y la Guardia Civil otorgan su máxima distinción a Pérez Rubalcaba |url=https://www.heraldo.es/noticias/nacional/2020/11/03/la-policia-y-la-guardia-civil-otorgan-su-maxima-distincion-a-perez-rubalcaba-1403365.html |access-date=2025-02-09 |website=[[Heraldo de Aragón]] |language=es}}</ref> In February 2025, the minister also granted him the Grand Cross of the [[Order of Merit for Security]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DM |first=EFE / |date=2025-06-17 |title=El Gobierno otorga a Pérez Rubalcaba la Gran Cruz de la Orden del Mérito a la Seguridad |url=https://www.eldiariomontanes.es/cantabria/gobierno-otorga-perez-rubalcaba-gran-cruz-orden-20250617202449-nt.html |access-date=2026-03-17 |website=El Diario Montañés |language=es}}</ref>
